SCIENCE PASSAGE 6: Origins of Bright Crater Rays
Three students discuss why some young impact craters have bright rays extending across the surface.

Student 1: The rays consist mainly of fresh material excavated from beneath a dark, weathered surface. With time, exposure to radiation and tiny impacts darkens the rays until they resemble the surrounding ground.

Student 2: The material is not intrinsically brighter. Impact fragments roughen the surface, and the rough texture reflects sunlight toward the observer at certain angles. As small grains settle, the directional reflection weakens.

Student 3: Both excavation and texture matter. Fresh subsurface material begins brighter than the surface, and rough fragment deposits enhance that contrast. Weathering and settling therefore work together to fade the rays.

Which statement describes a point of agreement among the students?

options.A: They agree that only a laboratory instrument can create the phenomenon.
options.B: They agree that the phenomenon never changes with time.
options.C: They agree that all competing explanations have already been disproved.
options.D: All three students agree that crater rays become less visually distinct over time.

questions.explanation: The stated point is consistent with every viewpoint.

Student 3: Both excavation and texture matter. Fresh subsurface material begins brighter than the surface, and rough fragment deposits enhance that contrast. Weathering and settling therefore work together to fade the rays.

Which prediction is most consistent with Student 3?

options.A: Changing either relevant factor could never affect the observation.
options.B: Student 3 would predict that both weathering of grains and smoothing of the deposit reduce ray brightness.
options.C: Only a factor that no student mentions could matter.
options.D: The phenomenon should remain perfectly constant over unlimited time.

questions.explanation: The prediction follows from Student 3’s combined-mechanism explanation.

SCIENCE PASSAGE 7: Battery Voltage at Different Temperatures
Students placed identical batteries in temperature-controlled chambers for 30 minutes. They then connected each battery to the same resistor and recorded voltage immediately and after 5 minutes. Each temperature condition used a new battery from the same package.

At 10, what was the absolute difference between Initial voltage and After 5 min?
questions.explanation: Read the two requested values and subtract; report the absolute difference.

SCIENCE PASSAGE 4: Pollinator Visits Through the Day
Observers counted visits to equal flower patches during four 30-minute periods. They recorded bee and butterfly visits separately. Weather remained clear, and the patches contained the same flower species and similar numbers of open blooms.

Which series had the greater value at 5 p.m.?

options.D: The figure does not contain values for that condition.

questions.explanation: Compare the two plotted values at the final x-position.

SCIENCE PASSAGE 5: Protective Coatings and Corrosion
Steel washers were cleaned, weighed, and coated with no coating, wax, paint, or a plant-based film. The washers were placed in equal volumes of saltwater for 10 days, dried, and reweighed. Greater mass loss indicates more corrosion. A second observation recorded the percentage of each surface covered by rust.

According to the figure, what value was recorded for Mass loss at Wax?
questions.explanation: Read the requested condition and series directly from the figure.
